$comment: The job this repository EXPECTS to carry a required status context, and what that job
must be performing for the expectation to mean anything.
Why a checked-in file at all: which checks branch protection actually requires is a
repository setting, and a pull request cannot read it. So the expectation is declared
here and the workflow hygiene lane checks the tree against this file. Reading live
settings is forbidden, because a check that cannot run on a pull request blocks nothing.
This file states an expectation. It cannot prove the setting agrees with it. What it can
do — and what the lane does — is make a change that would invalidate the expectation fail

why: `build` and not `ci-pass`. The aggregate verdict carries `if: always()` on purpose:
it has to run when its dependencies are SKIPPED, which is what a documentation-only
pull request produces. A declaration naming it would therefore assert two things at
once that cannot both hold — that the job carries no condition, and that it runs
when everything it needs was skipped.
The spec settles which job it is rather than leaving it to taste: the
executed-instance ceiling is written as 'at most four job instances while the job
named `build` carries the required status context, and at most three once that
context moves'. So `build` holds it today, moving it is anticipated, and this file is
verificationSet: Sanity grep — no internal spec IDs or version markers leak (post-build)
QFAI self-validate this repo (dogfooding — TDD gates)
QFAI self-validate this repo (dogfooding — SDD gates)
QFAI self-validate this repo (dogfooding — full profile)
Run qfai validate gate (fail on error)
verificationSetNote: Step names, because a step name is what a reader of the workflow sees and what a
reviewer of a diff notices moving. The lane accepts an item performed by the declared
job OR by a job it depends on, so relocating work into a dependency is legal and
relocating it out of reach is not.
The optional report upload is deliberately absent: it ends in a tolerated failure and
cannot fail the job, so it is not a verification however it is named.
